pluss::timeline::random¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::random(integer_range sizes,
                                 const Timeline& low,
                                 const Timeline& high,
                                 std::uint64_t seed = 0)

Sample Exact Instants From A Half-Open Interval¶

random() allocates a Timeline of sizes and independently samples every lane from the half-open interval [low, high). The lower bound can occur; the upper bound cannot. Half-open boundaries compose cleanly: adjacent intervals [a, b) and [b, c) neither overlap nor leave a gap.

Sampling operates directly on signed 64-bit epoch nanoseconds. It does not convert a broad time span through floating point, so neighboring nanoseconds remain distinct even when the endpoints are years apart. The output owns fresh, contiguous storage and carries the lower bound’s timezone metadata.

Use rand_between when the upper endpoint must be eligible or equal bounds should produce a constant result. random() instead requires high > low because [x, x) is empty.

Bounds And Shape¶

Both bounds must be defined scalar Timelines. Ordering is based on stored epoch nanoseconds, not displayed wall-clock fields. sizes may be empty for a scalar result or contain up to three non-negative extents. A zero extent is valid and produces an empty Timeline with the requested shape.

This factory accepts Timeline bounds only. That makes parsing and timezone projection explicit at the call site: use date(), time(), make(), or from_epoch() to build the exact interval you intend.

Seeds¶

A nonzero seed reproduces the same sequence for the same inputs and build. Seed 0 draws from the library seed stream and is intentionally not a request for a permanently repeated sequence. Tests and published examples should pass a nonzero seed.

The contract standardizes the interval and repeatability properties, not the particular random-engine sequence as a file format. Persist generated ticks if they must survive implementation upgrades exactly.

Example 1: A Scalar Shape And One-Tick Interval¶

const auto scalar = pluss::timeline::random(
    {}, pluss::timeline::from_epoch(0LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(1LL), 17);
std::cout << scalar.epoch_nanos() << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=0

Only tick 0 belongs to [0, 1), which makes both the scalar shape and the excluded upper endpoint visible without relying on probability.

Example 2: A Seeded Matrix¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::random(
    {2, 3}, pluss::timeline::from_epoch(10LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(15LL), 7);
std::cout << matrix.epoch_nanos() << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 12 14 11 ⎤
⎣ 11 14 11 ⎦

Every lane is at least 10 and less than 15; no lane can equal 15.

Example 3: Test The Contract Rather Than One Sequence¶

const auto matrix = pluss::timeline::random(
    {2, 3}, pluss::timeline::from_epoch(10LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(15LL), 7);
const auto repeated = pluss::timeline::random(
    {2, 3}, pluss::timeline::from_epoch(10LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(15LL), 7);

std::cout << (matrix.ge(pluss::timeline::from_epoch(10LL)).all().item<bool>() &&
              matrix.lt(pluss::timeline::from_epoch(15LL)).all().item<bool>())
          << '\n';
std::cout << matrix.epoch_nanos().equal(repeated.epoch_nanos()) << '\n';

Output¶

true
true

Example 4: Retain The Lower Bound’s Display Zone¶

const auto low = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-01T06:00:00Z")
                     .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto high = pluss::timeline::make("2024-07-01T06:00:00.000000003Z")
                      .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
const auto local = pluss::timeline::random({3}, low, high, 5);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(local, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000002-06:00", "2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000000-06:00", "2024-07-01T00:00:00.000000000-06:00"]

Example 5: Empty Geometry Is Still Valid Geometry¶

const auto empty = pluss::timeline::random(
    {2, 0}, pluss::timeline::from_epoch(0LL),
    pluss::timeline::from_epoch(1LL), 9);
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(empty) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[2, 0], tz=UTC)[  ]
[  ]

Failures And Cost¶

The call throws for equal or reversed bounds, absent bounds, non-scalar bounds, negative extents, rank above three, or shape-product overflow. Validation occurs before output values are produced. Runtime and storage are linear in the output numel().
